newsitem.title: USA: World Bnk rushes IDA graduation-St Kitts and Nevis.
newsitem.headline: World Bnk rushes IDA graduation-St Kitts and Nevis.

text.p: St. Kitts and Nevis representative Denzil Douglas Wednesday said the World Bank should reexamine its policies of graduating countries from concessional International Development Association lending to ensure that the guidelines are flexible.

Saying he was convinced that his country had been graduated too soon to more expensive World Bank loans, he said that a country should not be graduated until it was certain the country was on a sustainable path.

"We remain convinced that the decision to graduate the tiny vulnerable state of St. Kitts and Nevis from the use of IDA funds was premature," he told the annual meeting of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
He added that even after graduation has taken place, the Bank should continue to provide countries with technical assistance to help than stay on the right path.
He said that it had been the experience of his country that the donor community views IDA graduation as a signal for the reduction of development assistance.
"The fiscal, economic and social impact of such sudden and dramatic reduction of development assistance has been very severe and debilitating," he said.
